newsitem.title: FINLAND: Finnish pulp producers see higher prices - paper.
newsitem.headline: Finnish pulp producers see higher prices - paper.

text.p: Finnish forest industry groups Enso Oy and Metsa-Serla Oy expect pulp prices to rise five to 10 percent in May, business daily Kauppalehti reported on Friday.

"I don't see any reason why this would not happen... inventories are running down, paper consumption is good and no new capacity is coming," Kauppalehti quoted Enso Fibres' managing director Simo Pesola as saying.
Metsa-Serla marketing director Jyrki Yrjo-Koskinen agreed, the paper said.

The views were based on an expected 72,000 tonne rise in North American and Scandinavian so called Norscan pulp stocks in February to 2.13 million tonnes, and on expectations that Finns and North Americans will cut production, it said.
The current price of nothern softwood pulp is $520 to $540 per tonne, Kauppalehti said.
